_why: C2's footprint marks its anode ONLY with a band at local x=+2.2 and a 0.03 mm-radius dot at (+3.65,-2.15) - both sit under/at the edge of the 7.3 x 4.3 mm tantalum body, so on an assembled board C2 has NO visible polarity mark. C1's footprint already prints a 0.25 mm-stroke '+' clear of its body; C2 gets the equivalent. A reversed MnO2 tantalum on this rail fails SHORT, and there is no reverse-polarity protection by scope ruling. Placed above C2's anode (pad 1, +3V3, x=24.788): 0.42 mm clear of C2's silk body (top y=30.62), 2 mm from U1's pin-1 dot, 4 mm from U1's body outline.
